# Regulatory Reporting Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Regulatory Reporting Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 18 captured build checkpoints; 4 skills; 2 knowledge files; 9 acceptance checks; 4 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm tenant licensing and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved environment, publisher prefix and maker access. Confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model is available; keep the workshop synthetic and Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review uploaded report files, the proposed reporting connections and the intended channel; document blocked paths rather than bypassing them. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always authentication trigger; record who may build, test and use the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for the data lake, reporting workspace, SharePoint evidence library, Teams and filing connector, each with a dedicated least-privilege reference. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare reporting-lead, analyst, compliance, auditor and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: Copilot Studio in the browser and the reviewed files. Easy mode: VS Code Agent mode, the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin and a supported PAC CLI. | Customer or partner |
| Attestation and filing ownership | Have the regulatory owner name who attests source evidence and approves each filing action before real report data replaces the synthetic records. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Regulatory reporting owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Regulatory report status, data-quality exceptions and open audit findings by report Agree the starting portfolio and evidence gaps before attributing preparation or readiness changes to the agent.

Fill your baseline record:

| Report | Authority | Owner | Deadline | Status | Quality exceptions | Open findings | Measurement period |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Regulatory reporting owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Regulatory reporting owner | Approve source evidence and every filing action; confirm the authorized reviewers and production connections each response names. |
| Authorized report owners | Resolve validation exceptions and attest source evidence; certification and signature stay outside the agent. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and four skills; remove web search, confirm the model and record Draft state. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm licensing, capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before any reporting connection is approved. |
| Regulatory connection owners | Approve data lake, workspace, evidence library, Teams and filing-connector access through dedicated, least-privilege connection references. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check ENERGY_REGULATORY_REPORTING-01 through ENERGY_REGULATORY_REPORTING-04 and the boundary tests on the current Draft; reject partial-ingestion answers and inventory mismatches. |
| Operations owner | Own production monitoring, support and configuration recovery; route attestation and filing decisions to the authorized owners. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures for regulatory reporting have named agreement.
- [ ] The reporting owner records the current portfolio, deadlines and open findings before choosing success measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/energy-regulatory-reporting/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and confirm blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The approved environment and publisher prefix for the regulatory reporting build are recorded before a build lane is chosen.
- [ ] The customer approves the sign-in requirement, audience and least-privilege scopes for reporting data before any connection is bound.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/energy-regulatory-reporting/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/energy-regulatory-reporting/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/energy-regulatory-reporting/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/energy-regulatory-reporting/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Regulatory Reporting Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: energy-regulatory-reporting-rules-and-controls.md
7. Add knowledge: energy-regulatory-reporting-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: aibast_audit-readiness
9. Add skill: aibast_data-validation
10. Add skill: aibast_report-status
11. Add skill: aibast_submission-tracker
12. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
13. Open a fresh Preview conversation
14. Pass ENERGY_REGULATORY_REPORTING-01: Regulatory Reporting Lead
15. Pass ENERGY_REGULATORY_REPORTING-02: Data Analyst
16. Pass ENERGY_REGULATORY_REPORTING-03: Compliance Manager
17. Pass ENERGY_REGULATORY_REPORTING-04: Internal Auditor
18. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: ENERGY_REGULATORY_REPORTING-01, ENERGY_REGULATORY_REPORTING-02, ENERGY_REGULATORY_REPORTING-03, ENERGY_REGULATORY_REPORTING-04. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, environment, model, inventory, cases and Draft state.
- [ ] If the portable lane is chosen, the smoke test calls `RegulatoryReportingAgent` and returns its required markers.
- [ ] The manual build has reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, four skills and the confirmed model; web search and tools are absent.
- [ ] Each unchanged locked prompt passes once in its own fresh Preview conversation on the owned Draft.
- [ ] The deterministic validator decides each case; an annotated visual checkpoint does not replace it.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before any restricted reporting information is shown. Request only the scopes that approved report, workspace and evidence sources need. Restrict the audience and verify access with authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Approved regulatory data lake

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Regulatory connection owners

1. **Bind Approved regulatory data lake — read:** Bind scoped read-only connector or MCP tools.

2. **Identity for Approved regulatory data lake:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved regulatory data lake:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved regulatory data lake:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Do not certify or sign; give the screening result and state that an authorized report owner must resolve and attest evidence. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Say that it is absent and return no substituted report.

### Step 3-2. Integrate Controlled reporting workspace

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Regulatory connection owners

1. **Bind Controlled reporting workspace — read:** Grant read-only workspace access through an approved connector.

2. **Identity for Controlled reporting workspace:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Controlled reporting workspace:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Controlled reporting workspace:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Do not certify or sign; give the screening result and state that an authorized report owner must resolve and attest evidence. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim that a lookup, filing or update succeeded.

### Step 3-3. Integrate SharePoint evidence library

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Regulatory connection owners

1. **Bind SharePoint evidence library — read:** Add the approved library as knowledge with a content owner.

2. **Identity for SharePoint evidence library:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope SharePoint evidence library:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for SharePoint evidence library:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Do not certify or sign; give the screening result and state that an authorized report owner must resolve and attest evidence. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim that a lookup, filing or update succeeded.

### Step 3-4. Integrate Approved regulator filing connector

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Regulatory connection owners

1. **Bind Approved regulator filing connector — write:** Keep filing outside the agent; any workflow needs authentication, authorization, explicit approval and an audit record (preview).

2. **Identity for Approved regulator filing connector:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved regulator filing connector:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved regulator filing connector:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 1](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Refuse to file, sign or transmit; show recorded state read-only and name the authorized regulatory owner. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim that a lookup, filing or update succeeded.

### Step 3-5. Integrate Microsoft Teams for review and escalation

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Regulatory connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Teams for review and escalation — write:** Start without posting; gate any Teams message flow behind approval.

2. **Identity for Microsoft Teams for review and escalation:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Teams for review and escalation:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Teams for review and escalation:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 3](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): No prediction or legal advice; list open findings and severity only. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim that a lookup, filing or update succeeded.

### Step 3-6. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Regulatory connection owners

Bind least-privilege read connectors first; keep any write tool separate, with authorized confirmation, current-state validation and an immutable audit event.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Approved connections start as least-privilege reads; any later write tool stays separate from analysis.
- [ ] No lookup, filing or update is reported unless an approved production tool returns success evidence.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Test the approved deployment with reporting and denied identities; a maker's working connection does not prove other users' access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The business owner sets customer-data acceptance measures; synthetic scores, completeness and deadlines are not thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations name the tested version and user profile; General quality scoring does not replace exact reporting assertions.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked reporting corpus | All four cases, ENERGY_REGULATORY_REPORTING-01 through ENERGY_REGULATORY_REPORTING-04, return every required marker. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, four skills and the reviewed model; web search removed and no tools. |
| Regulatory authority boundary | Any signature, certification, transmission, filing-completion claim or audit prediction is no-go. |
| Visual checkpoint acceptance | Reusable captures show a positive deterministic anchor and no blocker; reshoot-required captures stay withheld. |
| Release state | Both validated agents remain Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Regulatory reporting owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Regulatory reporting owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The production publish operation has explicit human confirmation from the approval owner.
- [ ] The approved reporting audience and supported channels are tested before publication is confirmed.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review failed sessions, wrong-report answers, connection errors and credit usage in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Recovery is rehearsed with a restore path supported for the reporting environment type and target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, knowledge use, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.

## Deliverables Checklist

### Template provides

- [ ] Agent, synthetic data and component inventory.
- [ ] Integration/identity contracts and evaluation cases.
- [ ] Build-to-operate playbooks and integrity rules.

### Customer or partner delivers

- [ ] Adapted mappings, identities, governance and connections.
- [ ] Customer-data results, thresholds and go/no-go.
- [ ] Approved publication, operations and recovery.
